correctness.rationale: Definition 2.3 of arXiv:2604.14461v1 supplies the exact one-point-extension recursion. The four prime-extension kinds are exhaustive. Induction in RESULT.md proves the relative active-class/untouched-union lemma for every finite marked F; a second peeling induction and a sorting exchange yield the entire rooted-capacity rank criterion. The sharp minimum follows from t−1 capacity-forced rooted classes plus a rank-one two-point residual, which has exactly two isomorphism forms. Actual checker.py verified 1,215 unlabelled hosts, 2,325,866 individual marked-position threshold comparisons, 1,394 component-profile computations (1,215 exhaustive plus 179 additional samples), and both equality cases through rank six. Logs do not replace the universal induction.

originality.rationale: The closest accessible original 2026 rank paper defines and analyzes this single-host game but does not calculate the root-constrained equivalence-class capacity formula. Public neighbouring equivalence and idempotent-unary studies concern first-order quantifier-rank theory spectra, not the Kubiś–Shelah one-point-extension rank. Guingona–Parnes K-rank is a coding invariant of partial types. The pure-equivalence staircase is not a same-language implication: allowing at most one distinguished root creates two distinct mandatory new-class types, a root requirement within every active class, a rootless-final-witness exception and two sharp smallest hosts rather than one. This is a best-knowledge, not globally exhaustive priority assessment.
residual_risks: Historical priority is not independently established; inaccessible/unindexed results or forthcoming general rank work could contain a dominating formulation.

value.rationale: The exact one-point-extension rank of a natural hereditary class of rooted-partition structures is mathematically motivated by the 2026 rank framework. The theorem is a complete sorted-capacity classification for arbitrary finite hosts and a local criterion for every marked position; it yields exact t(t+3)/2 minimum thresholds and exactly two different extremal structures at each positive rank. The rootless-ordinary terminal exception is structural rather than a renamed pure-equivalence deduction and may support further analysis of enriched partition Fraïssé ranks.
